alerts.title: AKI on TDF with dehydration: consider TDF switch and assess renal function
alerts.message: Guidelines advise checking creatinine/eGFR in patients on TDF admitted with intercurrent illness, since dehydration or sepsis can cause renal deterioration. Renal impairment developing on TDF is managed by switching to ABC + 3TC + DTG. Patient creatinine rose from 0.9 to 2.4 mg/dL with urea 58 mg/dL, urea:creatinine ratio 24:1, pronounced volume depletion, and hypotension, which favours a prerenal/dehydration cause; TDF remains a plausible contributor given its nephrotoxicity, so attribution is not yet certain. Urinalysis shows no proteinuria or glucosuria, and stool microscopy is pending.

evidence.recommended_action: Continue IV rehydration and monitor creatinine/eGFR closely. If renal impairment persists or is attributed to TDF, switch to ABC + 3TC + DTG per guideline.

alerts.title: DTG creatinine rise assessment not yet documented
alerts.message: Guidance on creatinine rise on DTG distinguishes rises under 20 umol/L as likely DTG-related and rises over 30 umol/L as requiring further evaluation. The creatinine rise here (0.9 to 2.4 mg/dL, about 170 umol/L) far exceeds these thresholds, so DTG-related creatinine elevation alone cannot explain the event and the excerpt does not support attributing it to DTG; the rise is more consistent with acute kidney injury from dehydration and possible TDF toxicity.

evidence.recommended_action: Document the magnitude of the creatinine rise and reassess DTG contribution once renal function recovers and volume status is corrected.
